objectives: Students should use cumulative frequency graphs to determine how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds (Maths 6.1)
Students should interpret cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions (Maths 6.1)
Students should estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs (Maths 6.1)

keyConcepts.concept: Using cumulative frequency graphs to find values below or above thresholds
keyConcepts.explanation: Cumulative frequency graphs show the total number of data points less than or equal to a value, allowing us to find how many data values lie below or above any specific number.

keyConcepts.concept: Interpreting cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions
keyConcepts.explanation: By comparing cumulative frequency graphs of two or more sets of data, we can compare their spreads, medians, and overall distribution shapes.

keyConcepts.concept: Estimating median, quartiles and interquartile range (IQR) from cumulative frequency graphs
keyConcepts.explanation: Median and quartiles can be estimated by locating the 50%, 25%, and 75% points on the cumulative frequency graph. The IQR is the difference between the upper and lower quartiles.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: Cumulative frequency graphs help us understand how data accumulates up to certain values. They are useful to find how many data points fall below or above a threshold, as well as to estimate median and quartiles.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Using a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content: If a cumulative frequency graph shows 40 data points below value 30 and 70 data points below value 50, how many data points are between 30 and 50?

questions.question: How many data points lie between 30 and 50?
questions.explanation: The cumulative frequency below 50 is 70 and below 30 is 40. The number between 30 and 50 is 70 - 40 = 30.

steps.title: Dropdown Cloze: Estimating Median and Quartiles
steps.content:
Use the cumulative frequency graph to estimate the median and quartiles.

The median corresponds to the ___(1)___ percentile, which is the value where the cumulative frequency is ___(2)___. The lower quartile corresponds to the ___(3)___ percentile, and the upper quartile corresponds to the ___(4)___ percentile.

questions.text: The median corresponds to the ___(1)___ percentile, which is the value where the cumulative frequency is ___(2)___. The lower quartile corresponds to the ___(3)___ percentile, and the upper quartile corresponds to the ___(4)___ percentile.

steps.title: Summary Cloze: Understanding Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: Cumulative frequency graphs allow us to determine how many data points are below or above a value by reading the ___(1)___. The median is the value at the ___(2)___ data point. The interquartile range is found by subtracting the ___(3)___ quartile from the ___(4)___ quartile.

steps.title: Practice Question: Reading a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content:
A cumulative frequency graph shows there are 60 total data points. The cumulative frequency at value 40 is 20, and at value 70 is 45.

Questions:
1. How many data points are between 40 and 70?
2. Estimate the median value from the graph if the median corresponds to the 30th data point.
3. If the lower quartile corresponds to the 15th data point, estimate its value.

questions.question: 1. How many data points lie between 40 and 70?
2. Estimate the median value from the graph given the median corresponds to the 30th data point.
questions.answer: Value at which cumulative frequency reaches 30 (approximately)
questions.explanation: The median is found by locating 30 on the cumulative frequency axis and reading corresponding x-value from the graph.

questions.question: 3. Estimate the lower quartile value if it corresponds to the 15th data point.
questions.answer: Value at which cumulative frequency reaches 15 (approximately)
questions.explanation: The lower quartile corresponds to 25% of 60 = 15 data points; locate 15 on the cumulative frequency axis and read the corresponding x-value.
